good question! I am glad to answer:

different areas naturally have certain species growing there. weed didnt grow everywhere in the world. by introducing a non-native plant to an area, it can alter the biodiversity and species composition of an area by outcompeting the native species. even in a local area where something grows, it may only be native to that specific location. moving it 100miles could make it an invasive species to that area, if it fared well. by planting a species that is not normally there, it can prevent other species from growing by using the resources. understory plants are just as important as overstory trees. different wildlife rely on different species, and if some go extinct then some wildlife species may follow. this has been observed countless times all over the world. you may think that whats a few little plants in an entire landscape? thats what people used to think before we found out how damaging non-native species actually are to native populations. the problem is that it is not a fast process. it can take 5 years or it can take 50 years for something to change, but once it has, its extremely difficult to change back.

its actually quite interesting, most invasive species tend to be genetic specialists. meaning they are adapted to a specific set of conditions and will not do well outside of their natural habitat. however, they tend to outcompete genetic generalists, which can adapt to different conditions and locations. no one really knows why this is. but I digress.

if the weed took hold, there is no way of predicting what it would do. meaning controlled studies would have to be done to get a first step look of what would happen.

another example of humans fucking up nature is fire suppression in the US. maples have been dominating the understory on the east coast. human intervention in nature has caused fires to be stand replacing, meaning the fires burn with such an intensity that they destroy the live trees, making the area start over from the beginning. before humans, that never happened. but because humans put out fires that would have burned leaves on the ground, enough fuel builds up and is hot enough to destroy a forest.
